title: 13 Best Superblocks Alternatives in 2026
summary: Superblocks alternatives compared on self-hosting, SSO, audit logs and AI app generation: ToolJet, Appsmith, Windmill, Budibase, Retool and more.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Five of the 12 Superblocks alternatives after ours ship a free self-hosted edition: ToolJet, Appsmith, Windmill, UI Bakery and Budibase.
- Superblocks Teams is $100 a month billed annually, but SSO, audit logs, Git source control and VPC deployment are Enterprise-only.
- Retool closed self-serve self-hosting in February 2026, so a new self-hosted Retool starts with an Enterprise deal.
- Two of the 12 Superblocks alternatives, Microsoft Power Apps and Tray Helix, run only in the vendor's own cloud, and our product doesn't self-host either.


Superblocks alternatives are worth a look when you like its pitch, governed internal apps with an AI builder called Clark, but don't want SSO, audit logs and VPC deployment to wait for an Enterprise contract. If you're comparing Superblocks competitors for a security review, the first question is whether you can self-host, and on which plan.


Few ranking roundups answer that, so every tool below gets a column for it. All prices were re-checked on November 13, 2026.


We build[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) , and it's first because it's our product; it doesn't self-host. The other 12 are ordered by how far you can self-host with SSO, RBAC and audit logs without a sales call: free self-hosted editions, then DronaHQ's paid self-hosting, then four where self-hosting or a private cloud tenant needs an Enterprise deal or extra cost, then two that run only in the vendor's cloud.


## Why teams look past Superblocks


Superblocks isn't Enterprise-only, whatever older roundups say. Teams is $100 a month on annual billing, or $125 month to month, per team rather than per seat: up to 15 builders, unlimited end users, staging and production, RBAC and Clark. Superblocks has no free plan; you get a 14-day trial.


The friction starts with app count: Teams includes one hosted app, and each extra one adds $10 a month. SSO over SAML or OIDC, audit logs, Git source control and secrets managers all sit on the custom Enterprise plan.


AI has its own meter, Governed Agent Units (GAUs), pooled per organization and reset monthly. Teams includes 100 GAUs a month, and packs add more, from 100 GAUs at $100 a month billed annually up to 2,500 at $2,500. Superblocks' docs put adding a header at 1 GAU and building a full sales dashboard at 8.


Deployment is the last gate. Hybrid puts the data plane in your VPC on AWS, GCP or Azure, keeps production data there and lets Clark see only non-production data. Cloud-Prem runs the platform in your AWS account, managed by Superblocks, and Clark's inference goes through a Superblocks-run gateway unless you switch to your own Amazon Bedrock. Both are Enterprise-only; the default runs everything in Superblocks Cloud.


Superblocks keeps shipping, though. Version 3.0 (August 3, 2026) expanded imports from other AI tools or raw code and added security and policy agents plus a Smart Router that Superblocks claims cuts inference costs by up to 30%. Its FAQ lists SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA.


## The best Superblocks alternatives, compared


The last column gives each vendor's self-hosting answer in its own terms. Pricing (from) is the lowest entry point, rarely the plan with governance features.


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


A Yes in the last column can mean a free edition, as at Windmill, or a paid plan, as at DronaHQ.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Internal tools without a platform team


**Overview:** Superblocks gives a platform team the controls to govern internal apps. Awesomic, backed by Y Combinator, is for teams without one: AI agents build the apps, and vetted experts on a separate plan can finish them.


You get Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode as agents, billed together, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI. Each project runs on its own cloud computer, with storage up to 1 TB, where agents install, run and publish real programs such as an internal CRM.


Agents reach your data through 1,400+ app automations, and a shared team keychain lets teammates' agents use a key without seeing it. Admins see every prompt and result, set each person's access, approved models and budget, and track spend by person and model.


As for your data, the labs whose models our agents call are barred from training on it, though our Terms let Awesomic's own AI learn from de-identified content, with a forward-only opt-out.


**Key features:**


- Scheduled recurring work that runs without anyone starting it.
- Parallel agents, each in its own chat, on shared project files.
- Your own MCP servers beside the built-in connections.
- A share link for any project.


**Pricing:** Plans are chosen per person, and each price is that person's monthly AI budget: Studio at $499 for your heaviest builder, and Light at $19, Basic at $99 or Pro at $199 for everyone else. Experts are separate, with All-in-One priced at $3,219 monthly and a Dedicated expert quoted on a call.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**Pros:** Agents and experts in one app, tools that keep running on a cloud computer, 1,400+ app automations, an admin view of every prompt and result (no audit log is documented)


**Cons:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**How to start using it:**


1. Give the person who'll build most a Studio plan.
2. Start a project for your first internal tool.
3. Connect its apps and add their keys to the team keychain.
4. Set approved models and budgets for teammates.
5. For unfinished work, bring in a vetted developer on the Dedicated expert plan, right from the chat.


**Why it's a good Superblocks alternative:** It gets an internal tool built and kept running without a platform team to maintain it.


**Final verdict:** Choose Awesomic if you can work without self-hosting, SSO or an audit log; if not, ToolJet, Appsmith or Retool Enterprise fit better.[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) with one Studio plan.


### 2. ToolJet


**Overview:** ToolJet's Community Edition is free and open source under AGPL-3.0, so you can self-host before signing anything. Its paid plans build apps from a prompt.


**Key features:**


- An MIT-licensed MCP plugin, so Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can build ToolJet apps.
- Git sync, OIDC, LDAP and SAML SSO and 14 days of audit logs on Team, per its pricing grid.
- SCIM and air-gapped deployment on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Cloud Basic is $23 per builder a month on annual billing, or $29 month to month, and Team is $199, or $249 month to month. Self-hosted Team costs the same per builder.


**Pros:** Free self-hosted edition, one Team price anywhere, building from coding agents


**Cons:** End users capped at 50 or 100 below Enterprise, 2 builders on the free edition, workflows and Agent Builder self-hosted only


**Why it's a good Superblocks alternative:** SSO, audit logs and Git sit on a published plan you can self-host.


**Final verdict:** Start here for AI app building on infrastructure you control.


### 3. Appsmith


**Overview:** Appsmith's Community Edition is free and self-hostable under Apache-2.0, more permissive than AGPL. Its site now leads with Kite AI, a separate product from its founders, but Appsmith is still sold.


**Key features:**


- Custom roles, audit logs and unlimited Git repos on Business.
- SAML or OIDC SSO, SCIM and an air-gapped add-on on Enterprise.
- Appy, a copilot for queries, JavaScript and UI.


**Pricing:** Free covers up to 5 cloud users with Google SSO, and Business costs $15 a user monthly for teams of up to 99, cloud or self-hosted. Enterprise is listed at $2,500 a month, covering 100 users.


**Pros:** Apache-2.0 license, audit logs at $15 a user, SOC 2 Type II


**Cons:** SAML and SCIM start at $2,500 a month, Business stops at 99 users, the AI assists rather than builds apps


**Where it beats Superblocks:** Audit logs and Git come at a self-serve price, not a quote.


**Final verdict:** Pick Appsmith when cheap audit logs outweigh prompt-to-app building.


### 4. Windmill


**Overview:** Windmill is code-first, built so "engineers control what ships", and its free Community Edition is built on AGPLv3 source, with some proprietary code under a free-use license. Scripts, flows and apps share one tool, with copilots that run on your own model key.


**Key features:**


- SSO for up to 10 users on the free edition.
- Git sync, free for up to 2 users.
- AI copilots in scripts, flows and apps.


**Pricing:** The Enterprise Edition starts at $120 a month billed monthly, or $1,200 a year billed annually. Its monthly view charges $20 per builder, $10 per non-builder and $50 per standard worker.


**Pros:** Free edition with SSO, your own AI key


**Cons:** Audit logs, SAML and SCIM need Enterprise, seats-plus-workers pricing


**Who it suits best:** Engineers who'd rather write code than drag components.


**Final verdict:** Choose Windmill if developers build and a small Enterprise bill is fine.


### 5. UI Bakery


**Overview:** UI Bakery self-hosts on its Free, Team and Enterprise plans, air-gapped included. Its AI App Agent builds apps whose source code you can open and edit.


**Key features:**


- Custom roles and audit logs from Team.
- Editable source code behind AI-built apps.
- Hosted PostgreSQL for app data.


**Pricing:** A cloud developer seat is $20 a month billed annually, or $25 monthly, on Builder, and $35, or $40 monthly, on Team. Self-hosted Team costs the same, and self-hosted Enterprise adds your own AI key.


**Pros:** Self-hosting from the Free plan, AI output you can maintain as code


**Cons:** Custom SAML or OIDC SSO is Enterprise, the 51st cloud viewer seat forces Enterprise, self-hosted AI credits draw on the issuing cloud workspace


**What you get for the money:** Custom roles and audit logs at a public price, cloud or self-hosted.


**Final verdict:** Pick UI Bakery for AI-built apps you can still read, with 50 cloud viewers or fewer; if you self-host, confirm the seat cap with UI Bakery first.


### 6. Budibase


**Overview:** Budibase's open-source self-host is free for one workspace, with unlimited apps, automations, agents and users, SSO included. It's licensed under GPL v3, with paid features under BSL.


**Key features:**


- AI tables, AI columns, JavaScript generation and agents, but no prompt-to-app.
- Enforced SSO and user groups on Enterprise.
- SCIM, audit logs and air-gapped installs reserved for Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Cloud is one package from $299 a month, with 2 creators, 20 end users and 250K monthly actions. Extra creators cost $50 and extra end users $5 a month on annual billing, and monthly billing costs 20% more.


**Pros:** Free self-hosted SSO with no user cap, agents included, public cloud prices


**Cons:** Hard monthly action caps on cloud plans, audit logs and SCIM only on Enterprise, no Git page in its docs


**Why it earns a spot:** Free self-hosted SSO for any number of users, which Superblocks keeps for Enterprise.


**Final verdict:** Choose Budibase if SSO on your servers matters now and audit logs can wait.


### 7. DronaHQ


**Overview:** DronaHQ skips the free edition and sells self-hosting outright: self-hosted Business is $1,500 a month billed annually for 300,000 tasks. Its task-based cloud plans are flat, with unlimited users.


**Key features:**


- An AI app builder, with MCP access from Claude Code and Cursor.
- SAML or OIDC SSO and environments on Business.
- Granular permissions and audit logs on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Cloud Starter is $100 a month billed annually, or $140 monthly, for 25,000 tasks, and Business is $500, or $700 monthly, for 125,000. Extra tasks cost $0.002 each on every plan.


**Pros:** Unlimited users on its task-based plans, SSO below Enterprise, a public self-hosted price


**Cons:** Audit logs need Enterprise, self-hosted Business costs three times cloud Business on annual billing for 2.4 times the tasks, no permanent free plan


**The case for it:** Flat pricing pays off when many employees use what a few people build.


**Final verdict:** Pick DronaHQ if you want a published self-hosted price and can budget in tasks.


### 8. Retool


**Overview:** Retool's AI-native builder takes a request: "describe what you need, and it generates a working app". Self-hosting has narrowed: in a February 19, 2026 reply, a Retool staff member said it's "no longer accepting new self-hosted signups via our self-serve channel", though existing accounts continue.


**Key features:**


- Audit logs and external users on Business.
- SSO, SCIM, Git source control and your own AI key on Enterprise.
- Cloud, self-hosted or air-gapped deployment on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Free covers 5 users, Team is $10 per builder plus $5 per internal user a month billed annually, and Business is $50 plus $15.


**Pros:** Working apps from a prompt, self-serve audit logs, three deployment options on Enterprise


**Cons:** SSO, Git and self-hosting are Enterprise, internal users add to the bill, AI credits don't roll over


**When to pick it over Superblocks:** When self-serve audit logs matter now and the rest can wait.


**Final verdict:** Choose Retool if its cloud works for you; budget for Enterprise before you need your own servers.


### 9. Mendix


**Overview:** Mendix, part of Siemens, builds apps as visual models. Its agentic AI, Maia, can "execute complex, multi-step development tasks autonomously, from requirements to deployment".


**Key features:**


- Identity-provider integration for SSO on Standard.
- Kubernetes, private cloud or server deployment at extra cost, and air-gapped installs per its docs.
- High availability and horizontal scaling on Premium.


**Pricing:** Free has unlimited users and one environment per app, and Standard starts at $1,090 a month for one app or $2,725 for unlimited apps. Premium is quoted.


**Pros:** An air-gapped option, unlimited users on Free, AI that works inside visual models


**Cons:** Premium is quote-only, private deployment costs extra, Standard's SLA is 99.5%


**What sets it apart:** Private deployment options up to fully air-gapped, none of them on Free.


**Final verdict:** Pick Mendix for a long-running app program with budget for Standard or Premium.


### 10. Jet Admin


**Overview:** Jet Admin's AI builder generates apps from a prompt on credits, and "all plans include unlimited apps, unlimited users and unlimited workflows." Its FAQ lists SOC 2 Type II.


**Key features:**


- Two-way GitHub sync, environments and version control from Starter.
- Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs on Business.
- On-premise deployment with self-hosted AI models on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Starter is $20 a month billed yearly, or $25 monthly, and Business is $75 a month billed yearly, or $89 monthly. Free has limited credits.


**Pros:** Unlimited users on every plan, GitHub sync on the cheapest paid tier


**Cons:** On-premise needs an Enterprise quote, SSO and audit logs start at Business, credit rollover and top-ups are Enterprise-only


**Why governance teams shortlist it:** SSO, audit logs and Git all sit below Enterprise.


**Final verdict:** Choose Jet Admin for governance at a published price, if cloud hosting passes review.


### 11. Replit


**Overview:** Replit Agent builds apps from natural language, and Enterprise adds bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC), run in your cloud tenant and managed by Replit. Its docs say "Full BYOC does not mean an air-gapped or entirely self-hosted Replit installation": the control plane and Agent inference stay with Replit.


**Key features:**


- Replit Agent for plain-language builds.
- SAML SSO, SCIM, RBAC and audit logs on Enterprise.
- Single-tenant setups and private networking on Enterprise.


**Pricing:** Core is $18 a month billed annually, or $20 monthly, and Pro is $90, or $100 monthly, for up to 15 collaborators. Its docs describe a free Starter plan that the pricing page doesn't show.


**Pros:** Prompt-to-app building, a route into your own cloud tenant


**Cons:** Full BYOC is a private preview and not a self-hosted install, governance is Enterprise-only, credit pricing on Core and Pro


**Where it fits:** Prompt-first teams that will need their own tenant later.


**Final verdict:** Pick Replit if prompt-built apps come first and a managed tenant satisfies your security team.


### 12. Microsoft Power Apps


**Overview:** Power Apps runs only in Microsoft's cloud. In Microsoft's words, "Building apps is not charged, but using them requires paid licenses."


**Key features:**


- Environment-level governance and data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
- Dataverse Git integration with Azure DevOps or GitHub, per Microsoft Learn.
- Building by drag and drop, generative AI or code.


**Pricing:** Premium is $20 per user a month paid yearly, or $12 with a 2,000-seat minimum through sales, and the Developer Plan is free for non-production use. Extra Dataverse capacity costs $40 per GB a month.


**Pros:** A free Developer Plan, Git through Dataverse


**Cons:** Every production user needs Premium or pay-as-you-go, Microsoft's cloud only, limited Dataverse storage per license


**Who it's for:** Teams that govern through environments rather than servers.


**Final verdict:** Choose Power Apps if Microsoft's cloud is acceptable and you can license every production user.


### 13. Tray Helix


**Overview:** Tray Helix, from Tray.ai, doesn't build apps. You build in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and deploy to its managed runtime with one command. Its launch post called it an Early Access program, and access is still by request. Its pages list US, EU and APAC datacenters plus a Sovereign Cloud add-on.


**Key features:**


- One-command deploys from your coding agent.
- Enforced SSO, SCIM, 360 days of audit history, deployment approvals and rollback on Enterprise.
- "No seats, ever": per-workspace pricing plus usage.


**Pricing:** Builder Edition is $50 per workspace a month plus $1.00 per Helix Compute Unit, or committed rates. Enterprise is custom plus usage, with 500 HCUs a month included.


**Pros:** No seat pricing, deployment approvals and rollback on Enterprise, works with your current coding agents


**Cons:** Managed cloud only per its pages, a separate AI assistant does the building, full governance needs Enterprise, no free plan


**Why it's worth a trial:** It gives apps built in a coding agent a governed place to run.


**Final verdict:** Pick Tray Helix if your team already builds in Claude Code or Cursor.


## Self-hosting without a sales call


Retool's February 2026 change shows how fast a self-hosting answer can go stale. In a[Reddit thread on r/selfhosted](https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/comments/1rei4iy/retool_disables_selfhosted_pricing_plans/) , users said they found the change in Retool's docs with no announcement, and commenters called it a paywall on a core deployment option, quoting Retool's own admission that it hits smaller agencies. It's anecdotal, so check current docs.


Five tools still let you start on your own servers for free, and their editions differ: Budibase's covers unlimited users with SSO, while Windmill's caps SSO at 10 users and ToolJet's caps builders at 2 and end users at 50. Appsmith, DronaHQ, ToolJet, UI Bakery and Windmill publish a paid self-hosted price, so you can cost them without a call.


Past those prices, private deployment at Superblocks, Retool and Jet Admin is Enterprise-only, and Replit keeps the control plane under BYOC. A team that planned on self-hosted Retool now weighs an Enterprise deal against switching, and[our Retool roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/retool-alternatives) prices the alternatives.


## Where SSO and audit logs start, plan by plan


Self-hosting is half of governance. The other half is the plan where SSO and audit logs switch on, shown below for every tool except Mendix and Power Apps. We couldn't pin down Mendix's audit-log tier, and Power Apps governs through environments and DLP policies instead.


Prices are annual where a vendor shows both, except Windmill's monthly view. Five tools in the table put audit logs below Enterprise: ToolJet, Appsmith, UI Bakery, Retool and Jet Admin.


The billing unit moves the math more than the sticker. By our arithmetic, five builders and 20 internal users on Retool Business cost $550 a month billed annually, while Superblocks Teams covers up to 15 builders for $100, plus $10 per extra app, but leaves audit logs to Enterprise.


Usage is metered too: GAUs at Superblocks, pooled AI credits that don't roll over at Retool, AI credits at Jet Admin and tasks at DronaHQ, so price a month of real use. Seats need the same test: Appsmith's $15 Business seat stops at 99 users, and[our Appsmith alternatives guide](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/appsmith-alternatives) compares where to go past that.


## Shadow AI is the governance problem you already have


Governance matters more once AI is involved, because employees already use AI tools nobody approved. In a[Gartner survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-19-gartner-identifies-critical-genai-blind-spots-that-cios-must-urgently-address0) of 302 cybersecurity leaders, run March to May 2025, 69% of organizations suspected or had evidence that employees were using prohibited public GenAI.


Breach data points the same way: IBM's Cost of a Data Breach 2025, a Ponemon Institute study of 600 organizations, found that[13% reported breaches](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2025-07-30-ibm-report-13-of-organizations-reported-breaches-of-ai-models-or-applications,-97-of-which-reported-lacking-proper-ai-access-controls) of AI models or applications, and 97% of those breached reported having no AI access controls in place. Among organizations with AI governance policies, only 34% audit regularly for unsanctioned AI.


Past the access controls those breached firms lacked, an app builder's AI governance comes down to two questions: who holds the model contract, and where inference runs. Your own key moves the contract to you, at Windmill, Retool Enterprise and UI Bakery's self-hosted Enterprise.


Moving inference takes more: Superblocks Cloud-Prem can run it in your AWS account through your own Amazon Bedrock, and Jet Admin offers self-hosted models, both on Enterprise, while Replit keeps Agent inference even under BYOC. Awesomic's agents call hosted models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, so inference doesn't run on your servers.


## Tools we left off


A few names from other Superblocks roundups self-host only after a sales call, or not at all. OutSystems' paid plans are quote-only, and it offers on-premises deployment "in certain plans". Appian prices per user per app with no published figure, though it offers self-managed and on-premises deployment.


At the lighter end, Lovable has no self-hosted platform and puts SSO on Business, and none of Zite, Softr, Airtable, Noloco and Glide lists a self-hosted option on its pricing page. They suit a team portal better than a regulated internal app, and[our Softr roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/softr-alternatives) covers that end of the market.


## Mistakes to avoid with Superblocks alternatives


The first mistake is assuming a free self-hosted edition includes audit logs. None of the five here does: audit logs start on ToolJet Team, Appsmith Business and UI Bakery Team, and on Enterprise at Windmill and Budibase, so read the grid for the edition you'll install.


The second is counting builders your way, not the vendor's. At Retool, an analyst who fixes one label in an app counts as a builder for the whole billing cycle.


The third is ignoring end-user caps. On UI Bakery's cloud, viewer number 51 turns a cheap pilot into an Enterprise quote once the operations team logs in.


The last is treating "internal" as a reason to skip design. Employees can't pick another tool when a screen confuses them, and good[enterprise UX](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/enterprise-ux) pays back on an approval screen as much as on a product.


## How to choose the right Superblocks alternative


Start from the requirement your security team will check first, then narrow by who builds.


- With no license budget and a self-hosting deadline, test ToolJet, Appsmith, UI Bakery or Budibase, or Windmill if your builders write code.
- If audit logs on a published cloud plan are enough, compare ToolJet Team at $199 per builder, Appsmith Business, UI Bakery Team, Jet Admin Business and Retool Business.
- If the app must run air-gapped, shortlist UI Bakery's self-hosted plans, ToolJet Enterprise, Appsmith's air-gapped add-on, Budibase's Enterprise air-gapped deployment, Retool Enterprise or Mendix.
- If you already govern apps through Microsoft environments, pick Power Apps.
- If your team builds in Claude Code or Cursor, Tray Helix gives that code a managed runtime, with full governance on Enterprise.


If prompt-first building matters more than self-hosting, Retool, ToolJet, UI Bakery, Jet Admin and Replit are among those that generate apps from a description, and[our Replit roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/replit-alternatives) weighs more prompt-first builders.


Features may matter less than you'd expect. One team on r/selfhosted[migrating 307 applications](https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/comments/1opa6qh/looking_for_recommendations_on_selfhosted/) found Retool and ToolJet "almost identical" on granular RBAC, audit logs and SSO. It's one Reddit anecdote, but it suggests deployment and price often decide.


## Which Superblocks alternative to trial first


Pick two tools: one with a free self-hosted edition, and one on the exact plan your security review requires. Build the same small app in both, turn on SSO where the plan allows it, and check the paid plan's audit log against your security reviewer's questions.


Some internal tools are really scheduled jobs, such as a weekly client report, and our page on[scheduled jobs in connected apps](https://www.awesomic.com/apps/use-cases) shows how Awesomic runs them.


## FAQ


### Can you self-host Superblocks?


Only on Enterprise, through Hybrid, which keeps production data in your VPC, or Cloud-Prem, which puts the platform in your own AWS account, with inference on your own Bedrock if you switch it over. Its pricing FAQ also names GCP and Azure for Cloud-Prem, but its docs say AWS.


### What is the best free Superblocks alternative you can self-host?


ToolJet, Appsmith, Windmill, UI Bakery and Budibase each have one. All but UI Bakery's are open source: pick Budibase for free SSO with no user cap, or Appsmith for Apache-2.0, the most permissive of those four licenses.


### Which Superblocks competitors offer SSO without an Enterprise plan?


Budibase includes SSO free when self-hosted, and Windmill's free edition covers 10 users, with SAML on Enterprise. Appsmith Free offers Google SSO, leaving SAML and OIDC to Enterprise.


DronaHQ Business includes SAML or OIDC at $500 a month, and Jet Admin Business includes SSO at $75 a month, both billed annually. ToolJet's self-hosted Free adds Google and GitHub SSO, and its Team plan adds OIDC, LDAP and SAML at $199 per builder. Mendix puts identity-provider integration on Standard, from $1,090 a month.


### Can you still self-host Retool?


Existing self-hosted accounts continue, but Retool stopped accepting new self-hosted signups through its self-serve channel in February 2026. New self-hosted deployments now go through Enterprise, where SSO and Git also sit.


### What if the internal app has to run on phones?


This list of Superblocks alternatives judges how each tool deploys, not native mobile builds. Awesomic has iOS and Android apps for working with its agents, but a field team that needs a store-published app of its own should compare mobile builders separately, as[our Adalo roundup](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/adalo-alternatives) does.
